methodology.construction: A capitalisation-weighted index moves when market caps move. Each scored stock's point contribution = shares x (close - previous close) / divisor, where the divisor = the scored universe's total market cap at the previous close / the official index previous close. Rows are ranked by points; sector points are the sum of their stocks' points.
methodology.shares: Share counts = paid-up capital from the latest published quarterly filings compilation / Rs 100 par — the same share counts the filings' own EPS figures divide into. Counts refresh at quarterly compilations, so a bonus or right issue listed mid-quarter enters this board's weights at the next compilation.
methodology.prices: Raw traded closes from our OHLC archive — the basis the official index uses. A stock that did not trade on the session day carries its previous close and contributes exactly zero (flagged traded: false). On a stock's ex-date for a bonus/right issue the official divisor absorbs the mechanical price drop; this board's filings-based share count absorbs it only at the next compilation — one of the stated gap causes.
methodology.gap: The official index also counts listed symbols this board cannot score — companies without a compiled paid-up figure (mostly small caps), promoter shares and preference shares — and NEPSE adjusts its own divisor for new listings and corporate actions. Their net move plus those adjustments is the gap. It is printed on the page, never netted away.
methodology.tolerance: If the gap ever exceeds +/-7.5 points, or scored cap coverage of the official total market capitalisation falls under 85.0%, the daily build fails instead of publishing.
